To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of toxic substances can be classified into three types: (1) acute, (2) subacute, and (3) chronic.

(a) the effects of chronic exposure to toxic substances on the central nervous system are not necessarily dose-dependent; and (b) the effects of such substances on the central and peripheral nervous systems are interrelated.
The effects of chronic exposure to low doses of toxicants are not predictable from their acute toxicity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the study of threshold phenomena in toxicology is a very important task for industrial hygiene, and the study of threshold effects in the central nervous system is one of the most important tasks of this study.
we have been able to demonstrate that the toxic action of a substance can be determined by the intensity of its action and by the duration of the exposure to it.
the threshold effect is a phenomenon that occurs in the organism when the intensity of the action of a harmful factor is below the threshold of acute toxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no simple, direct relationship between the concentration of a toxicant in the environment and its effect on the organism.
the effects of the chemical on the brain can be measured in a relatively simple way and that this can provide a useful tool for assessing the potential toxicity of chemicals.
the threshold effect is a general principle that is applicable to all the functions of the central and peripheral nervous systems.
